Management Wants a Word - 9th August

Executive Summary & Challenge Briefing

Housekeeping retrieved a guest laptop left behind in Room 214, registered to "Vera". Before wiping the device for the next guest, IT pulled a full KAPE triage package. Hints scattered across her machine indicate that sensitive files were hidden behind multiple layers of Windows security and file-level encryption.

Key Hints & Analysis

  • Local Browser Secrets: Chrome stores saved passwords inside an SQLite database (Login Data), encrypted using AES-256-GCM.

  • DPAPI Master Key Protection: Chrome’s AES key is stored inside Local State and protected by Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI).

  • Credential Dumping: Vera’s Windows account password can be retrieved from local registry hives (SAM, SYSTEM, SECURITY).

  • VeraCrypt Storage: An encrypted file-container is located at C/Users/vera/Documents/backup.

Technical Methodology & Execution

Step 1: Locating Browser Artifacts & Analyzing Headers

We begin by inspecting the raw structure of the target container file and finding all relevant Google Chrome user data paths within the extracted KAPE triage directory.

Bash

xxd -l 64 ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera/Documents/backup

find ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera -type f \
  \( -iname 'Login Data' \
  -o -iname 'Local State' \
  -o -iname 'Web Data' \
  -o -iname 'History' \) -print
xxd -l 64 ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera/Documents/backup

find ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera -type f \
  \( -iname 'Login Data' \
  -o -iname 'Local State' \
  -o -iname 'Web Data' \
  -o -iname 'History' \) -print

Artifact Paths Identified:

  • .../User Data/Local State: Contains the DPAPI-encrypted AES key (os_crypt.encrypted_key).

  • .../User Data/Default/Login Data: SQLite database with encrypted URL passwords.

  • .../User Data/Default/Web Data: SQLite database with autofill metadata.

Step 2: Inspecting Stored Credentials via SQLite

Querying the logins table inside Login Data reveals the target login URL, stored username, and encrypted password blob:

Bash

sqlite3 '/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera/AppData/Local/Google/Chrome For Testing/User Data/Default/Login Data'

sqlite> SELECT origin_url, action_url, username_value, hex(password_value) AS encrypted_password FROM logins;

Step 3: Extracting Local Account Hashes & Decrypting DPAPI Master Key

To decrypt Chrome's state key, we need Vera's DPAPI MasterKey. We dump local system secrets using impacket-secretsdump against the Windows registry hives.

Bash

secretsdump.py \
  -sam ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Windows/System32/config/SAM \
  -system ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Windows/System32/config/SYSTEM \
  -security ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Windows/System32/config/SECURITY \
  LOCAL
secretsdump.py \
  -sam ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Windows/System32/config/SAM \
  -system ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Windows/System32/config/SYSTEM \
  -security ~/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Windows/System32/config/SECURITY \
  LOCAL

Extracted Credentials & User Data:

  • DefaultPassword (LSA Secret): minivera

  • User SID: S-1-5-21-2529683458-431225740-1723070931-1000

Step 4: Decrypting Chrome's AES Key

Extract the Base64 key payload from Local State, slice off the 5-byte DPAPI header prefix (tail -c +6), and decrypt the raw DPAPI blob in Python:

Bash

LOCAL_STATE="$(find "/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera" -type f -iname 'Local State' -print -quit)"

jq -r '.os_crypt.encrypted_key' "$LOCAL_STATE" | base64 -d | tail -c +6 > chrome-key.dpapi

MASTERKEY='5e5715ec9b6df5a86e97902692a66d28e691f05d5bc1e04d0159cfe960e94c978c07e5004a0179d3a96df2468885a28175b0b02cc064445f116a752d2b3e9d40'

python3 - "$MASTERKEY" <<'PY'
import sys
from impacket.dpapi import DPAPI_BLOB

masterkey = bytes.fromhex(sys.argv[1])
with open("chrome-key.dpapi", "rb") as f:
    blob = DPAPI_BLOB(f.read())

decrypted = blob.decrypt(masterkey)
with open("chrome-aes.key", "wb") as f:
    f.write(decrypted)

print(f"Decrypted Chrome AES Key: {decrypted.hex()}")
PY
LOCAL_STATE="$(find "/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera" -type f -iname 'Local State' -print -quit)"

jq -r '.os_crypt.encrypted_key' "$LOCAL_STATE" | base64 -d | tail -c +6 > chrome-key.dpapi

Step 5: Decrypting the Vault Password

With the 32-byte AES key recovered, we run an AES-256-GCM decryption script against the encrypted password blob inside Login Data:

Bash

LOGIN_DATA="$(find "/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera" -type f -iname 'Login Data' -print -quit)"

python3 - "$LOGIN_DATA" ./chrome-aes.key <<'PY'
import sqlite3, sys
from pathlib import Path
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

database = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
key = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve().read_bytes()
db = sqlite3.connect(database.as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True)

for url, username, encrypted in db.execute("SELECT origin_url, username_value, password_value FROM logins"):
    blob = bytes(encrypted)
    if not blob.startswith((b"v10", b"v11")): continue
    
    nonce, ciphertext_and_tag = blob[3:15], blob[15:]
    password = AESGCM(key).decrypt(nonce, ciphertext_and_tag, None).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    
    print(f"URL:      {url}")
    print(f"Username: {username}")
    print(f"Password: {password}")
PY
LOGIN_DATA="$(find "/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera" -type f -iname 'Login Data' -print -quit)"

python3 - "$LOGIN_DATA" ./chrome-aes.key <<'PY'

database = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
key = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve().read_bytes()
db = sqlite3.connect(database.as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True)

for url, username, encrypted in db.execute("SELECT origin_url, username_value, password_value FROM logins"):
    blob = bytes(encrypted)

    nonce, ciphertext_and_tag = blob[3:15], blob[15:]
    password = AESGCM(key).decrypt(nonce, ciphertext_and_tag, None).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    
    print(f"URL:      {url}")
    print(f"Username: {username}")
    print(f"Password: {password}")

Step 6: Mounting VeraCrypt Container & Retrieving Flag

Linux kernel cryptsetup supports VeraCrypt containers natively using tcryptOpen. We mount the file at C/Users/vera/Documents/backup using the decrypted password:

Bash

# Unlock the container
sudo cryptsetup tcryptOpen \
  --veracrypt \
  '/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera/Documents/backup' \
  vera_backup

# Passphrase: Wh4t1sV3raD0inG0nTh1sH0st

# Mount the exposed mapper device
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/vera_backup
sudo mount -t vfat -o ro /dev/mapper/vera_backup /mnt/vera_backup

# List contents
ls -la /mnt/vera_backup/secret_financial_documents
# Unlock the container
sudo cryptsetup tcryptOpen \
  --veracrypt \
  '/home/vps/Downloads/management-wants-a-word-forensics-hh-day-14/KAPE/C/Users/vera/Documents/backup' \
  vera_backup

# Passphrase: Wh4t1sV3raD0inG0nTh1sH0st

# Mount the exposed mapper device
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/vera_backup
sudo mount -t vfat -o ro /dev/mapper/vera_backup /mnt/vera_backup

# List contents
ls -la /mnt/vera_backup/secret_financial_documents

Retrieved Files:

  • transactions_q3.csv

  • important_invoice_byte_lotus.pdf

Copy the target document out of the read-only mount to read the final flag:

Bash

cp /mnt/vera_backup/secret_financial_documents/important_invoice_byte_lotus.pdf ~/important_invoice_byte_lotus.pdf

# Dismount and close device
sudo umount /mnt/vera_backup
sudo cryptsetup close vera_backup
cp /mnt/vera_backup/secret_financial_documents/important_invoice_byte_lotus.pdf ~/important_invoice_byte_lotus.pdf

# Dismount and close device
sudo umount /mnt/vera_backup
sudo cryptsetup close vera_backup
